01 / GET A WORKING COLLECTION

Start locally.

You need Git and Python 3.11 or newer. The lightweight demo uses sample garment drawings and simple image descriptors to check the retrieval workflow. It needs no GPU, API key or model download.

POWERSHELL / FROM A FOLDER YOU OWN
git clone https://github.com/sohitqwer-del/project-crumble.git
cd project-crumble
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\dev.ps1

The script creates .venv, installs the development dependencies, prepares a local demo workspace and starts the app. ExecutionPolicy Bypass applies to that PowerShell process.

Next time, run .\scripts\dev.ps1 -SkipInstall. Use -Port 8766 if the default port is busy.

SHELL / PYTHON 3.11+
git clone https://github.com/sohitqwer-del/project-crumble.git
cd project-crumble
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .
crumble --workspace work demo
crumble --workspace work serve

Linux is covered by the release workflow. Verify platform-specific model dependencies before production use on macOS.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 after starting the app. Open Photo search and upload a reference to retrieve up to four stored styles. Inspect each result and its images. The default demo encoder is a basic workflow check; use the fashion encoder for a real garment-search pilot.

02 / KEEP THE CONTEXT

Import your garments.

Use CSV or JSON Lines, with local image paths inside an explicit image root. Each garment has a unique ID. Keep brand, category, image rights and multiple views together.

Create garments.jsonl with one complete JSON object per line:

GARMENTS.JSONL / ONE RECORD
{"id":"dress-001","title":"Square-neck midi dress","brand":"Your studio","category":"dress","rights":"Our own photography","images":["dress-001-front.jpg","dress-001-back.jpg"]}

Put the two image files in a photos folder. Import into a new workspace with the fashion encoder after installing its optional dependencies:

ACTIVATED VIRTUAL ENVIRONMENT / CPU DEFAULT
pip install -e ".[fashion]"
crumble --workspace retailer init --encoder fashion
crumble --workspace retailer import garments.jsonl --image-root ./photos --report import-results.jsonl
crumble --workspace retailer worker
crumble --workspace retailer queue --limit 100
crumble --workspace retailer serve

Imports produce a per-record report. New images enter resumable embedding jobs. The worker processes them and publishes a search index. Add --watch to keep processing new jobs.

Your sources stay yours. Import imagery you have permission to use. The project does not bundle a retailer catalogue or a built-in retailer scraper. Brand names in your collection are source metadata, not project partners.

03 / MAKE THE COLLECTION SEARCHABLE

Choose the model deliberately.

The demo encoder is a simple image descriptor for testing the workflow. The optional fashion encoder uses a pinned public Marqo-FashionSigLIP revision for image and text embeddings. Its first use downloads model files.

An embedding is a numeric representation used to find visually related items. A high similarity score is not a match probability. Review the actual garment and the selected crop.

  • Use a new workspace to change the encoder or its version. Vectors from different models must not be mixed.
  • The default device is CPU. Choose --device cuda when initialising a fresh workspace only if your Python, PyTorch and GPU setup supports it.
  • Photo upload, drop, paste and manual crop are available in the full app. Text search needs the fashion encoder.
  • Visual part proposals need review. A full outfit can hide which garment produced a visual match.

Model and dataset terms are separate from the Apache-2.0 code licence. Review the model card and third-party notices for your use. This alpha has no established 98% accuracy claim.

04 / OPEN THE RETRIEVED RECORD

Keep the result connected to its source.

Each search result points back to a stored product. The interface shows its rank and the image view that matched the query. Open the product to inspect its other views and source details.

  • Retrieve up to four distinct product records. Fewer eligible records produce fewer results.
  • Multiple matching image views for one product are merged into one result.
  • Record identity, source URLs and image rights come from your imported metadata.
  • Snapshot and review history preserve earlier evidence when a record changes.

A similarity rank does not establish an exact match, garment launch date or copying relationship. Inspect the images before choosing a reference.

05 / WHAT IS STORED

Database, image files and vectors.

SQLiteProducts, source snapshots, image links, model identity, vectors and background job state.
Image filesOriented, resized JPEG working copies, stored by image-content hash.
Search indexA versioned generation of vectors and image IDs, with integrity checks.

The fashion encoder creates a normalised 768-value vector for each image view. New query images use the same model revision and preprocessing. Models or revisions with different identities are not mixed in the same index.

Default search compares stored vectors using cosine similarity. Optional FAISS HNSW provides approximate retrieval. A category filter selects eligible image views before exact scoring. Results are resolved back to product records, with duplicate views merged.

Index generations are published atomically: an unfinished rebuild does not replace the active search index. Embedding jobs resume after interruption. New images must be processed before they can appear in similarity search.

Stored images are working derivatives, not original-file backups. Keep original images in your own asset system.

07 / GROW WITH EVIDENCE

Local app. Optional heavier compute.

Run code, the reviewer and small collections on your own machine. A separately configured GPU machine can host model and data workloads. That requires an explicit deployment plan; the alpha does not include an automatic remote-GPU connector.

For a larger local catalogue, optional approximate retrieval is available:

OPTIONAL FASHION + HNSW BACKEND
pip install -e ".[fashion,ann]"
crumble --workspace retailer worker --max-jobs 1000 --index-backend hnsw --watch

Measure search recall, latency, index age, failed jobs and disk use on your collection. Multiple views create multiple vectors. The public application has not been validated as a million-item production service.

The current deployment is a pilot foundation. One organisation per workspace, one embedding worker and a shared access token. SSO, per-user roles, tenant isolation, distributed storage and high availability remain future work.

Keep the default loopback binding for local use. Remote access requires a strong CRUMBLE_TOKEN, exact allowed hostnames, HTTPS and reviewed proxy settings. See the deployment guide before exposing a workspace.

07 / BUILD IT IN THE OPEN

Help improve the system.

The code and original demo generator are Apache-2.0. There are no private retailer datasets, customer reviews or fine-tuned private model weights in the public package.

Useful contributions include garment retrieval evaluation sets with clear rights, reviewed match labels, model integrations, import tools, accessibility improvements and reproducible bug reports.

Contribution guide ↗Report an issue →

Report security issues through the repository's security policy rather than publishing credentials or sensitive garment data in an issue.
